sms-workflow-reminder-retry-count-tracki.text: The facts are right: the catch at scheduleSMSReminders.ts:189-197 does `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` for any error. A transient DB error is treated exactly like a transient Twilio error, which the PR also counts (`} else { ... retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, :179-186). The comment proposes a different retry policy; it does not show a defect.

dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex#.text: Each goroutine is bounded in time: dualwriter_mode3.go:51 `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, time.Second*10, ...)`, and the same appears at :110, :135 and :163. Because ctx derives from the request context, which is cancelled when the handler returns, most goroutines end even sooner. At most about write-rate × 10s goroutines can be outstanding, and each is a cheap goroutine holding one request object. Going from that to 'unbounded fan-out and memory growth' is a speculative capacity concern under hypothetical load, with no defect shown, so it is FP (none).

add-html-sanitizer-for-translated-messag.text: The behaviour is real, but it is a robustness point in a build-time verifier. The lowercase-only pattern is deliberate: the same file distinguishes uppercase pseudo-tags from HTML (`value.replaceAll("CLAIM\\.<[A-Z]*>", "")` :120, `value.replaceAll("<Extensions>", "")` :123), and `Pattern HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>");` (:139) relies on lowercase to tell markup apart from placeholders. No message bundle at head uses uppercase HTML tags, so nothing fails today. A hypothetical uppercase tag would be reported as 'Illegal HTML', which is the conservative direction for a sanitizer check, and the translator just lowercases the tag. That makes it a nit and not a defect that affects users.

authzservice-improve-authz-caching-grafa.text: The cache is trusted only for grants. When cached perms deny, Check does not answer from the cache: it falls through to `permissions, err := s.getIdentityPermissions(ctx, ...)` (service.go:139) and decides on fresh data. Labelling that request `permissionCacheUsage.WithLabelValues("false", ...)` (:137) therefore correctly records that the cache could not serve the decision. The label being named cache_hit does not make a 'found but insufficient, refetched' lookup a hit, and the metric is consistent with the design. The facts are right but there is no defect, so it is FP (none).

add-authzclientcryptoprovider-for-author.text: The leniency is real (tag & 0x1f), but no untrusted input reaches it. ASN1Decoder is package-private (`class ASN1Decoder {`, ASN1Decoder.java:33) and is used only in `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` (AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:128-134), which converts the DER signature just produced by the local JCA Signature.sign() into JWS R||S format during signing. Verification uses the encoder direction (concatenatedRSToASN1DER). A constructed INTEGER can only come from a broken local JCA provider, so the missing strictness has no practical effect. That makes it a nit and not a real input-validation defect.

Concede. The comment rests on 'a provider class name containing % ... would cause MissingFormatArgumentException and abort detection'. The providers come from `ServiceLoader.load(CryptoProvider.class, classLoader)` (CryptoIntegration.java:56), and ServiceLoader rejects any provider-configuration name that is not a valid Java identifier, which '%' is not. The described failure is impossible, and the rest (debugf vs debug, trailing comma) is cosmetic. The label is hallucination, and I adopt your severity.

optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.text: The comment itself says the schema and producer 'are assumed to guarantee a valid number'. The value is `end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]` (factory.py:141), taken from Relay-produced JSON on ingest-spans. Standard JSON has no NaN token, and the serializer of the producer does not emit one. A NaN therefore never reaches `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise ...})` (buffer.py:197-199) through any real path. A finiteness guard would only cover an unreachable state, so this is FP (none).
